_comment: Prebuilt third-party binaries. A fresh clone must compile no third-party code.

angle.sourceNote: Google publishes no ANGLE binaries and Expo ships none (expo-gl uses Apple's deprecated EAGL). Godot's static builds are the only public option. Shipping should build ANGLE in our own CI.

headers.refNote: The head of chromium/7578, and the commit the libraries report in GL_VERSION ('ANGLE 2.1.1 git hash: aaebda1c5a40'). Headers and libraries must come from one commit: gl-context asserts the match.
headers.note: Sparse checkout of include/ only (~1MB); no depot_tools needed.

apple-tvos-simulator-arm64.note: No tvos-simulator build exists upstream; derived from the ios-simulator archive by rewriting LC_BUILD_VERSION.

apple-tvos-device-arm64.note: No tvos build exists upstream; derived from the ios archive by rewriting LC_BUILD_VERSION.

unavailable.android-arm64: No public prebuilt ANGLE for Android exists. Android ships ANGLE as an optional system driver, not a linkable library. Android has universal native GLES 3.x, so ANGLE there is for driver normalisation only -- build from source if we decide we need it.

sdl3._comment: SDL3 is consumed prebuilt from the official release, never compiled. The runtime uses it for timers today (SDL_AddTimerNS owns event-loop scheduling); the window, input and audio subsystems arrive with their own specs.
sdl3.versionSource: libsdl-org/SDL release-3.4.16 -- the same release poc/build/sdl3-src is checked out at

apple.note: The .dmg carries one SDL3.xcframework with macos-arm64_x86_64, ios-arm64, ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator, tvos-arm64 and tvos-arm64_x86_64-simulator slices -- all genuinely built for their platform (the tvOS simulator slice reports LC_BUILD_VERSION platform 8), so retag-macho.py is never applied here. Headers live in each SDL3.framework/Headers, which is what makes #include <SDL3/SDL_timer.h> resolve.

android.note: The zip carries one SDL3-3.4.16.aar: prefab package SDL3 (module SDL3-shared; api 21, stl none) for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64, and a classes.jar with org.libsdl.app.SDLActivity, which the Android shell extends. It has no jni/ directory: libSDL3.so reaches the APK as a runtime file of the CMake target that links the prefab module. Only the .aar and the licence are kept from the zip.

unavailable.android-x86_64: In the .aar, and deferred by choice: the Android build targets the ABIs TV devices ship (deferred-work.md), so only android-arm64 and android-arm32 slice it.
unavailable.linux-x86_64: SDL publishes no Linux binary -- distributions package it instead, and the release page carries only source tarballs, the Apple .dmg, Windows VC/mingw archives and the Android .aar. Linux/Batocera is M11 and links the system libSDL3.so through pkg-config, which is the platform's own answer rather than a prebuilt.
unavailable.windows-x86_64: Published as SDL3-devel-3.4.16-VC.zip, but Windows is not a ScreenKit target -- not wired up.

sdl3_ttf._comment: SDL3_ttf is SDL's own font library, consumed prebuilt from the official release like SDL3 itself. The 2D canvas rasterises text through it (core/src/text): FreeType for glyphs and HarfBuzz for shaping, both linked inside the framework, so neither is a dependency of ours.
sdl3_ttf.versionSource: libsdl-org/SDL_ttf release-3.2.2 -- built against SDL 3.2, which the pinned SDL3 3.4.16 is ABI-compatible with

apple.note: One SDL3_ttf.xcframework with the same five slices as SDL3. Each framework links SDL3 through @rpath/SDL3.framework, so it loads the SDL3 the host already carries; FreeType and HarfBuzz are static inside it.

android.note: One SDL3_ttf-3.2.2.aar: prefab package SDL3_ttf (module SDL3_ttf-shared; api 19, stl none) for the same four ABIs as SDL3, with FreeType and HarfBuzz inside. It links libSDL3.so dynamically, so it uses the SDL3 the APK carries.

unavailable.android-x86_64: In the .aar, and deferred by choice: same as SDL3's.
unavailable.linux-x86_64: SDL_ttf publishes no Linux binary, like SDL itself. Linux/Batocera is M11 and links the system libSDL3_ttf.so through pkg-config.
unavailable.windows-x86_64: Published as SDL3_ttf-devel-3.2.2-VC.zip, but Windows is not a ScreenKit target -- not wired up.

hermes._comment: Hermes is consumed prebuilt from the React Native distribution, never compiled. This version IS the pin: hermesc and the engine must come from the same commit or the loader refuses the bytecode.

runtime.note: Root of the archive is destroot/. The framework is hermesvm, not hermes, and it exports the JSI implementation itself (466 facebook::jsi::* symbols) -- embedders link hermesvm alone and never compile jsi.cpp or vendor ReactCommon.

android.note: Kept as the .aar Gradle consumes. Prefab package hermes-engine, module hermesvm (api 24, NDK 27, c++_shared) for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64; jni/<abi> carries the stripped libhermesvm.so the APK ships. What it does not carry: the prefab excludes jsi/**, so include/jsi is copied from this Hermes's Apple destroot (byte-identical to React Native 0.88.0-rc.0's); and unlike the Apple framework, this hermesvm exports no JSI implementation -- it links libjsi.so and libfbjni.so. libjsi.so comes from the jsi block below. fbjni is com.facebook.fbjni:fbjni:0.7.0, the version this AAR's POM names, resolved by Gradle (runtime/android/gradle/verification-metadata.xml). Hermes's Intl on Android is Java, reached through fbjni.

jsi.source: com.facebook.react:react-android:0.88.0-rc.0 (Maven Central) -- the React Native release that pins this Hermes (hermes-compiler 260318099.0.2)
jsi.note: Only libjsi.so is kept, about 300-400 KB per ABI, each file checked against its own sha256 here; it needs nothing but libc++_shared.so. The rest of the AAR is React Native, which ScreenKit does not use, so it is read in memory and never written to the cache.

hermes.includeNote: Headers live ONLY here (jsi/jsi.h, hermes/hermes.h). The frameworks carry no Headers directory, so destroot/include must be on the header search path.

linux-arm64.slice: libhermesvm.so, aarch64 -- Raspberry Pi 3B+ and newer on a 64-bit OS
linux-arm64.intl: ICU 72 in lib/: Collator and DateTimeFormat are real; Hermes leaves NumberFormat and toLocale*Case as placeholders on Linux

linux-x86_64.intl: ICU 72 in lib/: Collator and DateTimeFormat are real; Hermes leaves NumberFormat and toLocale*Case as placeholders on Linux

android-arm64.slice: hermes-android .aar, prefab hermes-engine::hermesvm, arm64-v8a; libjsi.so from react-android

android-arm32.slice: hermes-android .aar, prefab hermes-engine::hermesvm, armeabi-v7a; libjsi.so from react-android

hermes.targetNote: Unlike ANGLE, Hermes publishes first-class tvos-arm64 and tvos-arm64_x86_64-simulator slices, so retag-macho.py is never applied here. macOS is a separate versioned framework under Frameworks/macosx -- the xcframework has no macos slice, only ios-arm64_x86_64-maccatalyst.

compiler._comment: hermesc moved out of the react-native tarball in 0.87. The npm package version is the Hermes version, which is what keeps compiler and engine on one commit.

linux._comment: React Native publishes no Linux runtime, so this one is ours: built from the same Hermes commit as the Apple framework and hermesc, by tools/prebuilts/recipes/hermes-linux/build.sh, and pinned here by sha256 like any other archive.
linux.source: facebook/hermes at the commit above, built by tools/prebuilts/recipes/hermes-linux
linux.urlNote: Not hosted yet. fetch.mjs takes the archive from $SCREENKIT_PREBUILTS_MIRROR or tools/prebuilts/dist/ (the recipe's output) until this is set; {asset} and {version} are substituted.

unavailable.windows-x86_64: No Hermes runtime is published for Windows; only the win64 hermesc host compiler, which the compiler block already covers.
unavailable.android-x86_64: Published, and deferred by choice: hermes-android and react-android both carry x86_64, but the Android build targets the ABIs TV devices ship (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a) and an arm64 Mac runs the arm64 emulator image. Adding it is a targets entry here and an abiFilter in runtime/android/app/build.gradle (deferred-work.md).
